title: Adaptive streamed robust Fourier-score Grover search: linear qubits, linear samples and 13/40 malformed fraction

claims.statement: For every integer N>=2 and every fixed hidden s in Z/NZ, let n=ceil(log2 N). The single streamed robust Fourier-score/Grover algorithm in proof.md uses M=2^18(n+1), threshold27/160, label error delta=1/(2^16 M), r=512 ceil(log2(4n/delta)), and 16 search trials with uniformly random iteration count below R=2^(ceil(n/2)+1). Under the fifth claim's adaptive malformed-copy error model with malformed fraction at most 13/40, it recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-1/256-2^(-16)-1/64>2/3. On every execution branch its total charged sequential work is T=O(2^(n/2)n^3 log_2 n), with absolute constants independent of N,s and the permitted adaptive adversary. This includes all classical bit operations, address charges, circuit generation, exact Clifford+T gates, source acquisition, initialization, measurements, failed trials and disposal. The full representative bit-length envelope is 2^(n/2)n^3 log_2 n and its exact growth index is1. These bounds hold jointly for this one configuration.

For every integer N>=2 and every fixed hidden s in Z/NZ, let n=ceil(log2 N). The single streamed robust Fourier-score/Grover algorithm in proof.md uses M=2^18(n+1), threshold27/160, label error delta=1/(2^16 M), r=512 ceil(log2(4n/delta)), and 16 search trials with uniformly random iteration count below R=2^(ceil(n/2)+1). Under the fifth claim's adaptive malformed-copy error model with malformed fraction at most 13/40, it recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-1/256-2^(-16)-1/64>2/3. On every execution branch it acquires exactly Q=M=2^18(n+1) fresh source copies, including all clean and malformed registers and all discarded registers. No source copies are acquired during search. Thus Q=O(n), with full representative envelope n and exact growth index0. All hidden constants are independent of N,s and the permitted adaptive adversary. These bounds hold jointly for this one configuration.

For every integer N>=2 and every fixed hidden s in Z/NZ, let n=ceil(log2 N). The single streamed robust Fourier-score/Grover algorithm in proof.md uses M=2^18(n+1), threshold27/160, label error delta=1/(2^16 M), r=512 ceil(log2(4n/delta)), and 16 search trials with uniformly random iteration count below R=2^(ceil(n/2)+1). Under the fifth claim's adaptive malformed-copy error model with malformed fraction at most 13/40, it recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-1/256-2^(-16)-1/64>2/3. The guaranteed malformed-sample fraction is epsilon(n)=13/40, meaning at most floor((13/40)Q) malformed deliveries for the deterministic Q=M. For every adaptive adversary permitted by the following complete model, including clean-only delivery, the same full-secret success guarantee and all four worst-case resource bounds hold jointly for this single configuration: Adaptive malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm, and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed; on every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. A malformed copy is an arbitrary (n+1)-qubit state (the register shape of an ideal copy) supplied from the adversary's system: it may be pure or mixed, may be entangled with the adversary's remaining system and with other malformed copies, and may depend on all of the information above; it is not entangled with clean copies or with the algorithm's workspace, ancillas or internal random bits. Every copy that is not malformed is clean: at the moment of its delivery, a fresh ideal coset state rho_s = (1/N) sum_x |psi_{x,s}><psi_{x,s}| in tensor product with everything else (the adversary's system, all other copies and the algorithm's workspace), i.e. clean copies are independent ideal coset states. The adversary interacts with the algorithm only by supplying copies; after delivery it has no access to the copy or to the algorithm's quantum or classical systems. All measurements have countably many outcomes. The algorithm is not told which copies are malformed. Quantifiers: the guarantee must hold for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold), every s in Z/NZ and every such adversary, including the adversary that corrupts nothing (the clean problem): the algorithm outputs the entire s with probability at least 2/3, and the four declared resource bounds hold on every execution branch. The fraction bounds the number of malformed copies among acquired copies; it is not a per-copy corruption probability.
